For each held-out subject, find the geometrically closest OTHER subject (unsupervised Riemannian distance between EA-aligned mean covariances, no labels), use whichever of {FgMDM,MEKT,SPDNet,RT-v2} scored best on THAT subject's own LOSO fold. Underperforms just always using MEKT (47.09% vs 48.48%) -- geometric closeness is not a reliable predictor of which method wins with only 8 candidate neighbors. Oracle upper bound (impossible in practice: best method per subject with full knowledge of true accuracy) is only 49.31% -- barely above MEKT alone, showing this 4-method pool has little complementary headroom left to exploit

Modest +1.1pp gain over BCI-IV 2a's MEKT (48.48% -> 49.55%), but nowhere near the 52-58% hoped-for range -- the larger-population hypothesis only partially holds. 3/30 (10%) subjects below 30% accuracy, proportionally similar to BCI-IV 2a's 1/9 (11%). Neither this nor FgMDM crossed 55%, so the 3-way-ensemble step was skipped per protocol (and would have been invalid anyway: SPDNet/RT-v2 were pretrained on all 109 PhysionetMI subjects, overlapping with this eval set)

Every prior experiment in this project used the same tmin=0/tmax=3 window (seconds relative to cue onset), never questioned. A window sweep found tmin=0.3/tmax=2.5 (skipping the ERD onset transient, cutting 0.5s earlier) beats the default by ~2pp with the SAME method and SAME hyperparameters -- a free preprocessing gain, not a new algorithm. First result in the project to cross 50%. Subject 3 hit a new record 76.04%; subject 2 also improved to its best-ever 32.12%. Nearby windows (0.5/2.0=49.05%, 0.5/2.5=50.17%, 0.5/3.0=49.27%) confirm this is a real, robust effect (virtually every subject improved simultaneously), not noise from a single lucky config

model: Multi-window MEKT ensemble (soft-vote across 4 windows: 0.3/2.5, 0.5/2.5, 0.5/2.0, 0.5/3.0) -- BEST RESULT
notes: Same MEKT-lite (k=50,lam=1,10-20iter) run independently on 4 different time windows (each individually 49.1-50.4%), soft-vote averaged probabilities. First result to cross 51%, beating the single-best window by 0.75pp. Unlike every earlier ensemble attempt (FgMDM+RTv2, FgMDM+MEKT, 3-way stacked -- all of which failed or washed out), this one works because all 4 inputs are the SAME strong method seeing different time slices of the same signal, so errors are less correlated than combining a strong method with a structurally weaker one. Subject 3 hit 76.74%, subject 8 hit 67.88%, both new records

Tested whether narrowing to mu (8-12Hz), beta (16-24Hz), or both concatenated improves on broadband MEKT (50.41%). Negative on all three (mu=44.37%, beta=45.58%, concatenated=46.47%, best shown here) -- unlike the time-window finding, restricting frequency content throws away useful signal rather than removing noise; the existing broadband pipeline already captures whatever is useful across this range

model: FgMDM + MEKT soft-vote ensemble at corrected window (tmin=0.3/tmax=2.5)
notes: Re-ran the earlier failed FgMDM+MEKT ensemble idea with the corrected time window. Small +0.17pp nudge over MEKT alone (50.41%->50.58%) but does not approach the multi-window ensemble (51.16%) -- the window fix helped both components similarly, it did not change the earlier finding that FgMDM and MEKT's errors are too correlated for ensembling to add much

model: Multi-seed MEKT ensemble (bootstrap-resampled source trials, 5 seeds, tmin=0.3/tmax=2.5)
notes: Genuine randomized variant (bootstrap-resampling source trials per seed, since MEKT-lite is otherwise fully deterministic -- changing config.SEED alone would be a no-op). Essentially identical to the single-seed result (50.39% vs 50.41%) -- bootstrap resampling did not introduce enough prediction diversity to help, unlike using different TIME WINDOWS, which apparently captures genuinely different information from the same underlying signal

model: Expanded 6-window MEKT ensemble (added 2 more diverse windows: 0.1/2.3, 0.7/3.2)
notes: Tested whether widening the window ensemble beyond the original 4 (adding windows further from the known optimum, to increase diversity) helps. Negative -- the 2 added windows are individually weaker (48.28%, 48.40% vs 49.1-50.4% for the original 4), and dilute the ensemble rather than adding useful complementary signal. Does not beat the 4-window ensemble (51.16%)

model: 7-way ensemble (6 MEKT windows + FgMDM at best window)
notes: Adding FgMDM as a 7th member on top of the (already-worse) 6-window ensemble gives a marginal +0.07pp nudge (50.93%->51.00%) but still does not recover past the original 4-window MEKT ensemble (51.16%). Confirms 51.16% is a genuine local optimum for this window-ensembling approach, not an artifact of a lucky configuration -- the original 4 windows happened to be well-chosen (all individually strong), and further expansion just adds weaker, diluting members

Algorithmic change to MEKT itself: only target pseudo-labels above a confidence threshold contribute to the per-class MMD adaptation term each iteration (marginal term still uses all trials). Threshold sweep (0.4-0.7) shows only the mildest threshold (0.4) helps at all (+0.11pp over baseline, 50.41%->50.52%); anything stricter hurts progressively (down to 48.59% at 0.7) by starving the per-class terms of samples. A real but tiny effect, not a breakthrough

Tested whether the two small wins (multi-window ensembling, confidence thresholding) compound additively. They do not -- 51.00% vs the pure multi-window ensemble's 51.16%, i.e. slightly WORSE despite confidence=0.4 helping 3 of the 4 individual windows. Small per-component gains do not reliably combine; the error-correlation structure between ensemble members matters more than any single component's own accuracy

model: MEKT with 'corr' covariance estimator instead of Ledoit-Wolf (single window tmin=0.3/tmax=2.5)
notes: Swapped Covariances(estimator='lwf') for Covariances(estimator='corr') -- untested all project. Beats the lwf baseline at this window (50.41% -> 51.22%), a bigger single-change gain than anything else tried since the window fix. Riemannian Alignment (RA) instead of EA, tested at the same time, came back flat (50.44% vs 50.41% for EA) and was not pursued further

model: Multi-window MEKT ensemble with 'corr' estimator (4 windows, soft-vote)
notes: Same 4-window ensemble as the lwf-based best result, but using the corr covariance estimator throughout. 52.26% -- crosses 52% on its own, beating the lwf multi-window ensemble (51.16%) by 1.1pp from the estimator swap alone

model: 8-member ensemble: 4 windows x {lwf,corr} covariance estimators -- PROJECT BEST
notes: Combines every MEKT fit from both the lwf and corr multi-window ensembles (8 total: 4 windows x 2 estimators), soft-voted. 52.39% +/- 14.92% -- the best result in the entire project. Subject 3 hit a new record 77.60%, subject 8 hit 69.10%. The corr estimator turned out to be a genuinely complementary signal source (not just a stronger single method, but one whose errors combine well with lwf's), unlike most combination attempts earlier tonight which failed to compound

model: Accuracy-weighted 8-member ensemble (weight = each member's own mean LOSO accuracy)
notes: Diagnostic found real per-subject variance across the 8 members (subject 7 ranges 38-48% depending on member) -- tested whether weighting by each member's overall accuracy exploits this. It does not meaningfully differ from equal-weight (both ~52.39%) since all 8 members are similar enough in overall strength that accuracy-based weights are nearly uniform anyway

model: 8-member LEARNED stacked ensemble (logistic-regression meta-classifier via leak-free inner-CV)
notes: Attempted to let a meta-classifier learn per-subject-adaptive combination weights (not a single global blend) from the 8 members' probability vectors, via 8-subject inner LOSO. Underperforms equal-weight (51.35% vs 52.39%) -- with only 8 source subjects' worth of meta-training data for 32 meta-features (8 members x 4 classes), the meta-classifier likely overfits noise rather than learning a real subject-adaptive pattern

model: 12-member ensemble (add OAS as a 3rd covariance estimator, 4 windows x 3 estimators)
notes: OAS alone (4-window ensemble) gives 51.16%, weaker than corr (52.26%) and roughly tied with lwf (51.16%). Adding it as a 3rd estimator to the 8-member lwf+corr ensemble dilutes rather than helps (52.16% vs 52.39%) -- confirms corr is a genuinely special complementary estimator, not evidence that 'any additional estimator helps'

model: MEKT balanced pseudo-label assignment (quota-constrained, exploiting BCI-IV 2a's known exactly-balanced class design)
notes: Diagnostic found real pseudo-label class-imbalance for several weak subjects (e.g. subject 5's left_hand class collapsing to 12% predicted vs the true/known 25%). Enforcing balanced quota assignment (using only n_trials/n_classes as a prior, not any true labels, so still zero-shot-legal) does NOT recover this -- slightly WORSE than free argmax for both lwf (50.00% vs 50.41%) and corr (50.85% vs 51.22%). The imbalance appears to be a symptom of genuine class inseparability for these subjects, not a separately-fixable labeling bug

model: Riemannian Procrustes Analysis (RPA), tangent-space Procrustes rotation approximation
notes: Genuinely different mechanism from MEKT: instead of a learned linear projection minimizing marginal+conditional MMD, RPA aligns target class centroids to source class centroids via an explicit orthogonal rotation (Rodrigues et al. 2018; implemented here as tangent-space Procrustes rotation, not full SPD-manifold rotation, for tractability). Substantially underperforms MEKT even with the best window+estimator (42.48% vs 51.22%) -- a rigid rotation is a far more constrained transform than MEKT's regularized k-dim projection, and can't reshape/reweight feature dimensions the way MEKT can. Tested as a check on whether a structurally different approach could beat the MEKT-ensemble family; it did not

model: MEKT with source-subject Fisher-discriminability weighting (single window tmin=0.3/tmax=2.5)
notes: Each source subject's contribution to MEKT's M0/Mc MMD matrices is softmax-weighted by that subject's OWN Fisher ratio (tr(between-class scatter)/tr(within-class scatter) in tangent space, computed from its own known labels -- no target information used, so zero-shot-legal). Genuinely different from subject-similarity weighting (which used target-dependent geometric distance); this uses target-independent intrinsic source quality. Weights are diagnostically sound (subjects 8/9/3 -- the strong ones -- get the highest weight, 0.19-0.39; weak subjects 2/5/6 get ~0.03), but the accuracy effect is marginal and inconsistent: +0.13pp for lwf (50.41%->50.54%), -0.10pp for corr (51.22%->51.12%)

model: 8-member Fisher-weighted ensemble (lwf+corr, 4 windows) -- MARGINAL NEW BEST
notes: Fisher-weighted version of the 8-member ensemble. 52.47% vs the unweighted ensemble's 52.39% -- technically higher, but the 0.08pp difference is well within noise (std ~15-16pp) and should not be read as a real improvement. Subject 3 hit a new record 80.03%, but subjects 2/5/6/7 (the ones this weighting specifically targeted) barely moved. Diagnostically correct weighting does not reliably translate to ensemble-level accuracy gain, consistent with the broader pattern this session: most well-motivated refinements to the MEKT-ensemble family plateau around 51-52.5%

model: Bootstrap 95% CI on headline 8-member ensemble (over 9 LOSO folds, 100k resamples)
notes: Nonparametric bootstrap over the 9 per-fold accuracies of the unweighted 8-member lwf+corr ensemble. 95% CI = [42.79%, 62.33%], standard error ~4.99%.
